title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Overhead Projector. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Overhead Projector
options.thesis: The page is one transparency on the glass: source on the left, what it becomes on the right.
options.viewport: A lit sheet fills the frame; the Markdown source sits in the left half and its rendered chapter on the right, with the machine's lamp switch as the only button.
options.risk: The projector is an object: if it becomes a picture of a projector instead of a working page, it is costume.

raised.raise: State is a physical mark, never a hue: one red grease tick is the page's only signal that a draft is unsaved.
Every demonstrated thing carries a provenance ticket — chapter, source, bundled or linked.
Measure is authored per block: the rendered column narrows and widens with its content instead of one global width.
Code, then decode: the left pane is always the code that produces the right pane.
A ranked legend instead of a feature list: symbols in the order a teacher needs them.

options.label: The Exercise Sheet
options.thesis: The product as the sheet a teacher hands out: numbered tasks, ruled space, one pencil mark.
options.viewport: One sheet on a desk, filled: the exercise and its answer space side by side, and a rubber-stamped action in the corner.
options.risk: Familiar: the handout is the first thing anyone would try for a classroom product; only the craft can carry it.

options.label: The HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: One card, two modes: what you read is what you can edit, one keystroke apart.
options.viewport: A white card with hand-drawn borders on a dithered desk, the document on it, and buttons that turn the page.
options.case: Fuses cleanly on clarity — reading and editing are the same object — but a teacher does not identify with a 1987 Mac.
options.risk: Reads as nostalgia unless the card system does real work.

options.label: The Cutting Bench
options.thesis: A perforated rail of frames, with state kept as marks: grease cross, tape flag, hung trim.
options.viewport: One rail crosses the sheet, the lesson frames strung along it, the place you stopped flagged.
options.risk: A film bench is not a teacher's world; the page would explain editing, not writing.
options.kept: State as a mark, not a hue.

options.label: The Moon-Shadow Bazaar
options.thesis: Documents traded as shadows, each tagged with where and when it was cast.
options.viewport: A lane of stalls at night, each shadow carrying a ticket of origin and length.
options.risk: Invention with no audience: nobody recognises a market that does not exist.
options.kept: A provenance ticket on everything demonstrated.

options.label: The Coiled Tower
options.thesis: Writing as courses of clay: each band's measure set by what it carries.
options.viewport: Courses rise up the page, each line's measure matching its band.
options.risk: Beautiful and mute: the metaphor does not say what the product does.

options.label: The Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: The page as a numbered catalog entry: matte black, a white plot, a colour code that spells the name.
options.viewport: A black sleeve with one white line stack and a fac number as the only headline.
options.risk: Speaks to designers, not teachers; the code has to be decoded before the page means anything.

options.label: The Orienteering Map
options.thesis: A fixed colour language beneath, a numbered course above, and a legend that ranks the symbols.
options.viewport: Terrain in flat ISO colour, the purple course riding over it control to control.
options.risk: A map is a route, not a document; the colour language fights whatever world carries the page.
options.kept: A ranked legend instead of a feature list.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Dark hero, browser screenshot, three feature cards, a GitHub button: what every editor ships, done well.
canonCard.viewport: Eyebrow, headline, subcopy, two buttons, a laptop mockup, then a three-card row cut by the fold.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
